subject: future

sources.title: Selective dopamine D3 receptor antagonism by SB‐277011A attenuates cocaine reinforcement as assessed by progressive‐ratio and variable‐cost–variable‐payoff fixed‐ratio cocaine self‐administration in rats
Ratio and time requirements on operant schedules: effort‐related effects of nucleus accumbens dopamine depletions
A Systematic Analysis of Infinite Scrolling in Digital Interfaces: A Good Accompanied by Bad and Ugly

facts.claim: Dopamine depletions in the nucleus accumbens increase the tendency for rats to take long pauses in responding of more than 20.0 s.
facts.quote: DA depletions also increased the tendency to take long pauses in responding (i. e. > 20.0 s), and this effect was evident across all schedules tested.

facts.claim: In rats, the drug SB-277011A blocks cocaine-enhanced brain stimulation reward and cocaine-seeking behavior.
facts.quote: In rats, acute administration of SB-277011A, a highly selective dopamine (DA) D(3) receptor antagonist, blocks cocaine-enhanced brain stimulation reward, cocaine-seeking behaviour and reinstatement of cocaine-seeking behaviour.

facts.claim: SB-277011A failed to impede locomotor activity, impair rearing behaviour, produce catalepsy, or impair rotarod performance in rats.
facts.quote: SB-277011A (3, 12 or 24 mg/kg) failed to impede locomotor activity, failed to impair rearing behaviour, failed to produce catalepsy and failed to impair rotarod performance.

facts.claim: Dopamine in the nucleus accumbens appears to be necessary for adapting to work-related response costs that provide a challenge to the organism.
facts.quote: Attachment of ratio requirements to interval schedules is a work-related response cost that provides a challenge to the organism, and DA in nucleus accumbens appears to be necessary for adapting to this challenge.

facts.claim: The drug SB-277011A reduces the cocaine dose-response break-point curve produced by a 24 mg/kg dose.
facts.quote: The reduction in the cocaine (0. 25-1. 0 mg/kg) dose-response break-point curve produced by 24 mg/kg SB-277011A is consistent with a reduction in cocaine's reinforcing efficacy.

facts.claim: Infinite scrolling is a widely adopted feature that transforms how users interact with and consume content.
facts.quote: Infinite scrolling has emerged as a widely adopted feature, transforming the way users interact with and consume content.

research.angle: While dopamine is linked to reward and work-related challenges in rats, these sources do not provide evidence linking infinite scrolling to neurological fatigue or gambling-like dopamine patterns in humans.
research.verdict: The sources provide data on dopamine receptors and rat behavior, but they do not connect these biological mechanisms to the specific mechanics of infinite scrolling.
research.caveat: The research on dopamine and rewards is conducted in rats and does not directly measure human behavior or digital interface usage.
